Independent finite replay method: for m=3,...,12, enumerate masks from 0 to 2^(m+1)-1, reject adjacent bits, group by exact Lucas sum and record the size and presence of both bits 0 and 2 for each mask; assert each group has at most two masks and compare the full excess histogram among pairs. The frozen replication entry point is CHECK.py, for m=3,...,24.
correctness.rationale: Canonical subsets partition into the disjoint intervals below and above L_m and give each integer in [0,L_(m+1)-1] once. Redundant subsets have distinct sums by highest-differing-index dominance on their tails beginning at index 4. A maximal initial even run ending at 2j+2 telescopes to L_1+L_(2j+3); the unchanged tail begins no earlier than 2j+5. This gives excess j, and the cutoff admits the partner exactly when m>=2j+3. At equality the empty tail contributes F_1; thereafter the path-independent-set count gives F_(m-2j-2). Summation gives the stated parity correction and reindexing gives the bivariate generating function. Binet estimates give geometric domination, so the limiting mean and variance follow by moment convergence, not just pointwise convergence of probabilities. Separate bounded enumeration matched the full histograms and representation multiplicity assertions for 3<=m<=12; for m=12 the histogram is (55,21,8,3,1).
residual_risks: The independent enumeration is bounded and is not used to prove the theorem beyond its enumerated cutoffs. No formal proof certificate or expert attestation was verified.
